thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Struggle Amid Ongoing Trade Concerns, But Apple Leads Tech Rebound

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Struggle Amid Ongoing Trade Concerns, But Apple Leads Tech Rebound
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
As 2018's second half starts, industrials and materials hit as trade-war fears aren't going away
U.S. stocks mostly fell on Monday, opening the third quarter of 2018 on a negative note as trade tensions between the U.S. and its major trading partners continued to show signs of escalating.
The day's losses were widespread, with the energy and material sectors among the biggest decliners of the day, but technology stocks inched higher and provided some support, briefly lifting the Nasdaq into positive territory.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 85 points, or 0.4%, to 24,185. The S&P 500 lost 4 points to 2,715, a decline of 0.1%. The Nasdaq Composite Index was at break-even levels at 7,513.
Trading could be volatile this week, as some market participants will be out of the office for the Fourth of July holiday, for which markets will be closed on Wednesday. Lower trading volume can exacerbate day-to-day swings.
Read:Which markets are closed for July Fourth? (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/which-markets-are-closed-on-july-4th-2018-07-02)
What's driving markets?
Recent trading in both directions has been driven by uncertainty over trade policy, with investors seeking clarity about how protectionist changes to U.S. policies could be, as well as whether such changes will be met by severe retaliatory measures. A trade war is seen as providing a significant headwind to global growth.
On Sunday, President Trump said he sees his threat to impose global auto tariffs as his biggest weapon (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-says-threat-of-auto-tariffs-is-biggest-weapon-in-trade-disputes-2018-07-01) to extract concessions from trading partners. At the same time, he called the EU "as bad as China" in hindering U.S. trade.
Meanwhile, a Financial Times report (https://www.ft.com/content/38388ebe-7d21-11e8-8e67-1e1a0846c475) on Sunday said the European Union has threatened $300 billion in fresh tariffs against U.S. products if Trump follows through on his threatened 20% levies targeting the trade bloc's auto makers. And Canadian retaliatory tariffs took effect Sunday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/canada-begins-imposing-tariffs-on-126-billion-of-us-goods-2018-07-01), with those measures serving as a response to U.S. metals tariffs.
In another significant question mark, Axios reported that the Trump administration had crafted a draft bill (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/leaked-draft-bill-indicates-trumps-intention-to-dump-wto-report-2018-07-02) that would declare America's abandonment of World Trade Organization rules. This would essentially give Trump a license to raise tariffs at will, without congressional consent and largely outside of the international rules governed by the WTO.
Don't miss:Trade-war fears? These lower-risk stocks are weathering the market storms (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trade-war-fears-these-lower-risk-stocks-are-weathering-the-market-storms-2018-06-30)
And see:Here's the key question for U.S. investors about the trade skirmish with China (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-the-key-question-for-us-investors-about-the-trade-skirmish-with-china-2018-06-29)
What are strategists saying?
"That we're starting the second half of the year on a down note is really telling. This is usually a slow week with the holiday, but there's definitely color in the market that is causing it to be volatile," Mark Esposito, president of Esposito Securities, a Dallas-based asset manager.
"When Trump starts talking about the WTO, China, all these big economies and these big threats, the market is going to react to that. It creates turmoil, and people are getting frustrated with all the back and forth. I think the long-term growth story of the economy remains intact, but in the meantime the trade will can cause a lot of tremors in the short term," he said.
What are other markets doing?
European stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-drive-lower-as-trump-hints-at-targeting-eu-with-tariffs-2018-07-02)were retreating, after Asian markets finished mostly lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stocks-in-japan-china-slip-as-asian-markets-take-cautious-start-to-new-quarter-2018-07-01).
Oil futures (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-slide-after-trump-tweet-hints-at-bigger-production-rise-from-saudis-2018-07-02)fell after a weekend tweet from Trump hinted at a big potential production increase (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-says-saudi-arabia-agreed-to-raise-oil-output-by-maybe-up-to-2-million-barrels-a-day-2018-06-30) from Saudi Arabia. Gold futures also were down, as the ICE U.S. Dollar Index gained.
Which stocks are in focus?
Among the biggest trade-related stocks to see heavy action, Boeing Co. (BA) fell 0.7%, while 3M Co. (MMM) was off 1%.
On the upside, Apple Inc. (AAPL) rose 0.7%, helping to lift tech stocks into slightly positive territory; the group had previously dropped as much as 1%. Among other stocks, Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) rose 0.9% and Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) rose 0.3%.
Auto-industry players such as General Motors Co.(GM)and Ford Motor Co.(F)were also in focus on trade concerns. GM on Friday warned the Trump administration (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gm-warns-tariffs-could-hurt-its-business-raise-cost-of-cars-2018-06-29) that tariffs on vehicle imports would hurt its competitiveness, cost U.S. jobs and result in "a smaller GM."
Other major auto makers joined GM in comments to the U.S. Department of Commerce, including Toyota Motor Corp.(7203.TO) (7203.TO), which warned Friday that auto tariffs "would have a negative impact on all manufacturers."
GM lost 0.1%, while Ford was down 0.6%. U.S.-listed shares of Toyota were down 0.8%.
United Rentals Inc. (URI) agreed to acquire BakerCorp (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/united-rentals-to-acquire-bakercorp-for-about-715-million-in-cash-2018-07-02) International Holdings Inc. for about $715 million in cash. Shares fell 1.1%.
Alkermes PLC (ALKS) rose 0.8% after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved its long-acting injectable (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/alkermes-stock-jumps-3-premarket-after-fda-approves-injectable-schizophrenia-treatment-2018-07-02) atypical antipsychotic for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults.
Adamis Pharmaceuticals Corp. (ADMP) jumped 34% after it announced a distribution and commercialization agreement with Novartis AG's (NOVN.EB) Sandoz Inc. unit.
Compugen Ltd. (CGEN) jumped 6% after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration lifted a clinical hold (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/compugen-shares-surge-12-premarket-after-fda-lifts-clinical-hold-on-cancer-treatment-2018-07-02) on its investigational new drug application for an immuno-oncology therapeutic antibody.
Which economic reports are in focus?
A read on June manufacturing from Markit came in at 55.4, compared with a preliminary reading of 54.6. Separately, the Institute for Supply Management's manufacturing index rose to 60.2% in June from 58.7%. A read on construction spending rose 0.4% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/construction-spending-ticks-up-in-may-as-housing-takes-a-breather-2018-07-02) in May.
